source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 1: Evaluate six determinants, parts (i)-(vi) (book page 58).

blocks.explanation:
A numerical \(3 \times 3\) determinant: we must find one number, its value.
There is no zero and no common factor that helps, so we expand along row 1.
Plan: three minors of row 1, signs \(+,\,-,\,+\), add.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & -4 \\ 3 & -1 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\)
To find: the value of \(\Delta\).
Method: Expansion along row 1: \(\Delta = a_{11}A_{11} + a_{12}A_{12} + a_{13}A_{13}\), where each cofactor is \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\). For row 1 the signs are \(+,\,-,\,+\).

Minor \(M_{11}\) (cover row 1, column 1)
\[M_{11} = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -3 \\ 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(2) - (-3)(3)\]
\[= -2 + 9 = 7\]
Why: A \(2 \times 2\) determinant is (leading diagonal product) minus (other diagonal product).

Minor \(M_{12}\) (cover row 1, column 2)
\[M_{12} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & -3 \\ -2 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (3)(2) - (-3)(-2)\]
\[= 6 - 6 = 0\]
Why: \((-3)(-2) = +6\), so the two products are equal.

Attach the signs and add
\[\Delta = 1(7) - (-2)(0) + (-4)(7)\]
\[= 7 + 0 - 28\]
\[= -21\]
Why: The cofactors of row 1 are \(+M_{11},\ -M_{12},\ +M_{13}\); each entry of row 1 is multiplied by its cofactor.

Check (expand along column 1)
\[\Delta = 1(7) - 3\begin{vmatrix} -2 & -4 \\ 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix} + (-2)\begin{vmatrix} -2 & -4 \\ -1 & -3 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 7 - 3(8) - 2(2)\]
\[= 7 - 24 - 4 = -21 \;\checkmark\]
Why: A determinant has the same value whichever row or column we expand along. Here \((-2)(2) - (-4)(3) = 8\) and \((-2)(-3) - (-4)(-1) = 2\).

blocks.explanation:
A numerical \(3 \times 3\) determinant; we must find its value.
No row or column has a zero, so we expand along row 1.
Plan: minors \(M_{11}, M_{12}, M_{13}\), signs \(+,\,-,\,+\), add.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 10 & -1 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\)
To find: the value of \(\Delta\).
Method: Expansion along row 1 with signs \(+,\,-,\,+\): \(\Delta = 5M_{11} - 2M_{12} + (-3)M_{13}\).

Minor \(M_{11}\)
\[M_{11} = \begin{vmatrix} 10 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (10)(-2) - (-1)(1)\]
\[= -20 + 1 = -19\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 1; what is left is this \(2 \times 2\) determinant.

Minor \(M_{12}\)
\[M_{12} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (3)(-2) - (-1)(-2)\]
\[= -6 - 2 = -8\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 2. Note \((-1)(-2) = +2\), and we subtract it.

Minor \(M_{13}\)
\[M_{13} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 10 \\ -2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (3)(1) - (10)(-2)\]
\[= 3 + 20 = 23\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 3; minus a negative is plus.

Attach the signs and add
\[\Delta = 5(-19) - 2(-8) + (-3)(23)\]
\[= -95 + 16 - 69\]
\[= -148\]
Why: Each entry of row 1 times its signed minor (cofactor).

blocks.explanation:
A numerical \(3 \times 3\) determinant; we must find its value.
Row 1 has small numbers, so we expand along it.
Plan: three minors, signs \(+,\,-,\,+\), add.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ -1 & 3 & 5 \\ -2 & 5 & 6 \end{vmatrix}\)
To find: the value of \(\Delta\).
Method: Expansion along row 1: \(\Delta = 1\cdot M_{11} - 2M_{12} + (-3)M_{13}\).

Minor \(M_{11}\)
\[M_{11} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 18 - 25 = -7\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 1; \(3 \times 6 = 18\), \(5 \times 5 = 25\).

Minor \(M_{12}\)
\[M_{12} = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 5 \\ -2 & 6 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(6) - (5)(-2)\]
\[= -6 + 10 = 4\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 2; minus a negative is plus.

Minor \(M_{13}\)
\[M_{13} = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 3 \\ -2 & 5 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(5) - (3)(-2)\]
\[= -5 + 6 = 1\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 3.

Attach the signs and add
\[\Delta = 1(-7) - 2(4) + (-3)(1)\]
\[= -7 - 8 - 3\]
\[= -18\]
Why: Row 1 entries times cofactors \(+M_{11},\ -M_{12},\ +M_{13}\).

Check (row operations)
\[R_2 + R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 + 2R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(0 - 18) = -18 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Adding a multiple of one row to another does not change a determinant (Property vii). Column 1 then has one non-zero entry, so only \(1 \times (5 \cdot 0 - 2 \cdot 9)\) remains.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Evaluate the following determinant: \(\begin{vmatrix} a+b & a-b & a \\ a & a+b & a-b \\ a-b & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
A letter determinant; we must simplify its value to a short expression in \(a\) and \(b\).
Each row adds up to the same total \(3a\), so adding the columns gives a common factor.
Plan: \(C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\), take \(3a\) out, make zeros, expand.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} a+b & a-b & a \\ a & a+b & a-b \\ a-b & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\)
To find: the value of \(\Delta\).
Method: Properties of determinants. Adding columns to a column does not change the value (Property vii); a common factor of a column comes outside (Property v). This avoids long bracket products.

Add all columns into column 1
\[C_1 + C_2 + C_3 \to C_1\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 3a & a-b & a \\ 3a & a+b & a-b \\ 3a & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1: \((a+b) + (a-b) + a = 3a\); rows 2 and 3 also give \(3a\), because \(+b\) and \(-b\) cancel.

Take \(3a\) out of column 1
\[\Delta = 3a\begin{vmatrix} 1 & a-b & a \\ 1 & a+b & a-b \\ 1 & a & a+b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Every entry of column 1 has the factor \(3a\) (Property v).

Make zeros in column 1
\[R_2 - R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 - R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = 3a\begin{vmatrix} 1 & a-b & a \\ 0 & 2b & -b \\ 0 & b & b \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: New \(R_2\): \((a+b) - (a-b) = 2b\), \((a-b) - a = -b\). New \(R_3\): \(a - (a-b) = b\), \((a+b) - a = b\). Subtracting a row does not change the value.

Expand along column 1
\[\Delta = 3a \cdot 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 2b & -b \\ b & b \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 3a\,[2b^2 - (-b^2)]\]
\[= 3a \cdot 3b^2 = 9ab^2\]
Why: Only the entry 1 in column 1 is non-zero; its position \((1,1)\) has sign \(+\).

Check with numbers
\[a = 2,\ b = 3:\ \begin{vmatrix} 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 5 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 5(27) + 1(9) + 2(9) = 162\]
\[9ab^2 = 9(2)(9) = 162 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Row 1 expansion: \(5(25+2) - (-1)(10-1) + 2(4+5)\). Both values agree, so the formula is right.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(9a^2b - b^3\) for part (iv). This is wrong: for \(a = 2,\ b = 3\) it gives \(108 - 27 = 81\), but the determinant equals \(162\). The correct value is \(9ab^2\).

blocks.explanation:
A numerical \(3 \times 3\) determinant; we must find its value.
Many entries are negative, so we write every product in brackets.
Plan: expand along row 1 with signs \(+,\,-,\,+\).
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 20 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\)
To find: the value of \(\Delta\).
Method: Expansion along row 1: \(\Delta = 1\cdot M_{11} - 20M_{12} + (-2)M_{13}\).

Minor \(M_{12}\)
\[M_{12} = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(-1) - (-3)(2)\]
\[= 1 + 6 = 7\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 2.

Minor \(M_{13}\)
\[M_{13} = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1)(4) - (-1)(2)\]
\[= -4 + 2 = -2\]
Why: Cover row 1 and column 3.

Check (row operations)
\[R_2 + R_1 \to R_2,\quad R_3 - 2R_1 \to R_3\]
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 20 & -2 \\ 0 & 19 & -5 \\ 0 & -36 & 3 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1[(19)(3) - (-5)(-36)]\]
\[= 57 - 180 = -123 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Row operations of this type keep the value (Property vii); then column 1 has only one non-zero entry.

blocks.prompt: 1 (vi) Evaluate the following determinant: \(\begin{vmatrix} 2x & x & x \\ y & 2y & y \\ z & z & 2z \end{vmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
A letter determinant; we must simplify it.
Row 1 has the factor \(x\), row 2 the factor \(y\), row 3 the factor \(z\).
Plan: take \(x, y, z\) out of the rows, then evaluate the number determinant.
steps:
Given: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 2x & x & x \\ y & 2y & y \\ z & z & 2z \end{vmatrix}\)
To find: the value of \(\Delta\).
Method: Property v: a common factor of a row can be taken outside the determinant. Then only a simple number determinant is left.

Take the factors out of the rows
\[\Delta = xyz\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: \(x\) from \(R_1\), \(y\) from \(R_2\), \(z\) from \(R_3\); each comes out once.

Expand along row 1
\[= xyz\,[2(4 - 1) - 1(2 - 1) + 1(1 - 2)]\]
\[= xyz\,(6 - 1 - 1)\]
\[= 4xyz\]
Why: Signs \(+,\,-,\,+\); minors \(\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 3\), \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 1\), \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -1\).

Check with numbers
\[x = y = z = 1:\ \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 4\]
\[4xyz = 4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Putting simple values in both sides is a quick test of a letter answer.
